items.title: Phil Woods — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: INTERVIEWER: Thomas? That sounds… I don’t I don’t know. [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah, but Chapin, I knew …

ctx.x: Thomas? That sounds… I don’t I don’t know.

Yeah, but Chapin, I knew … Anyway, the dad was a drummer, a great drummer, and he had a jazz band. Billy Byers was the trombone player, I was the alto player, Don Stratton was the trumpet player. We used to work Monday nights and I got to I moved to Brooklyn which is where the Goodsteins, the people who owned Birdland, and they kind of took me under their wing. They used to bring me food and stuff like that, you know, as a kid, and tryin’ to make my way, and I was hired to do the Birdland All-Stars in 1956. But…
